candidates.attacker_control: Remote unauthenticated HTTP client controls (a) the Content-Type header of a POST request — Dispatcher.wrapRequest treats any value containing 'multipart/form-data' as multipart, and commons-fileupload 1.3.2 reports the rejected content type in its InvalidContentTypeException message (dependency behavior, not readable here); (b) the multipart file name in Content-Disposition, which JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.addFileSkippedError embeds verbatim into the FileSizeLimitExceededException message when the request size exceeds struts.multipart.maxSize; and (c) explicitly the 'args' values that are formatted into messages.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked and rejected the following counterevidence/excuses: (1) struts-messages.properties does define struts.messages.upload.error.SizeLimitExceededException and .IOException, so attacks must use a different exception type — the bundle has no entry for InvalidContentTypeException, FileSizeLimitExceededException, FileUploadException, IOFileUploadException, etc., and JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest's key prefix is even misspelled (singular), so findDefaultText reliably fails; (2) the evaluation only happens when the action is ValidationAware — this is the common ActionSupport case and is a prerequisite, not a mitigation; (3) fileUpload must be in the stack — it is in the default stacks shipped in struts-default.xml; (4) for the default 'jakarta' parser the attacker-controlled part of the commons-fileupload 1.3.2 exception text could not be read from this snapshot (jar is a binary dependency outside the tree), so the in-repo-provable attacker control rests on the JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest file-name message; the content-type variant is inferred from the documented S2-045 mechanism and the identical code path.
candidates.impact: Remote code execution in the context of the web application (the evaluated expression runs with the full capabilities of Struts' OGNL/value-stack machinery, not merely a reflected error string), plus disclosure/DoS side effects from expression evaluation. This is the classic pre-fix Apache Struts multipart parser RCE class (S2-045/S2-046, CVE-2017-5638).
candidates.prerequisites: A deployed Struts application whose action stack includes the fileUpload interceptor (part of struts-default.xml defaultStack/completeStack, lines 299 and 332) and whose action implements com.opensymphony.xwork2.interceptor.ValidationAware (e.g. extends ActionSupport) so that validation.addActionError(...) and thus LocalizedTextUtil.findText(...) is reached. Default struts.multipart.parser=jakarta (default.properties line 69); the fully in-repo attacker-controlled message path uses the alternative jakarta-stream parser (struts.multipart.parser=jakarta-stream). No authentication is implied.
candidates.root_cause: Multipart parsing failures are converted into LocalizedMessage objects whose defaultMessage is the raw exception message (e.getMessage()), which can embed attacker-controlled request data (Content-Type for the default 'jakarta' parser, and directly the multipart file name in JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.addFileSkippedError: "Skipped file " + fileName + "; request size limit exceeded."). FileUploadInterceptor.intercept then calls LocalizedTextUtil.findText(clazz, textKey, locale, defaultMessage, args). When the key is not found in any resource bundle (true for most exception class names; struts-messages.properties only defines SizeLimitExceededException and IOException, and JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest even uses the key prefix 'struts.message.upload.error.' with singular 'message'), LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage falls back to defaultMessage and calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack), which evaluates ${...}/%{...} against the ActionContext value stack via OGNL. The Dispatcher wrapper condition only requires the Content-Type to *contain* 'multipart/form-data', so a header such as '%{(...)}...multipart/form-data' reaches the parser and its error message.
candidates.title: Attacker-controlled multipart parse error message is evaluated as an OGNL expression (S2-045/S2-046-style RCE)
candidates.trace: HTTP POST with malicious Content-Type (contains 'multipart/form-data') -> Dispatcher.wrapRequest (Dispatcher.java:800-804) -> MultiPartRequestWrapper ctor -> JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse (JakartaMultiPartRequest.java:83) catches FileUploadException -> buildErrorMessage (116-120) creates LocalizedMessage(this.class, 'struts.messages.upload.error.<SimpleClassName>', e.getMessage(), args) where e.getMessage() carries the attacker content type -> FileUploadInterceptor.intercept (260-266) calls LocalizedTextUtil.findText(error.getClazz(), error.getTextKey(), locale, error.getDefaultMessage(), error.getArgs()) -> findMessage finds no bundle named after the multipart class/package and findDefaultText(key) misses because struts-messages.properties (lines 34-36) only defines SizeLimitExceededException and IOException -> LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage (LocalizedTextUtil.java:714-737) takes defaultMessage and calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) at line 729 -> TextParseUtil.translateVariables (TextParseUtil.java:46-48) evaluates ${...} and %{...} via ValueStack.findValue -> OGNL evaluation of attacker text (RCE). The in-repo fully-verified variant replaces the first exception with JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.processUpload -> addFileSkippedError (350-357), which formats the attacker-supplied file name into the exception message, and buildErrorMessage (511-515) uses the singular key prefix 'struts.message.upload.error.', which cannot match the bundle, guaranteeing the default-message evaluation branch.
candidates.unverified: The exact exception message produced by commons-fileupload 1.3.2 for the default parser path was not readable in this snapshot; OGNL evaluation was not executed (no code execution permitted), so impact is reasoned from the presence of translateVariables over a live ValueStack, not runtime-confirmed. Whether this snapshot is precisely the parent of the fix for this chain (versus an already-mitigated-by-bundle state) could not be confirmed from repository metadata.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-917 Expression Language Injection / CWE-94 Code Injection (unsafe evaluation of attacker-controlled error text)

coverage_summary: Read the multipart stack end to end (Dispatcher.wrapRequest, MultiPartRequestWrapper, JakartaMultiPartRequest, JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest, MultiPartRequest, LocalizedMessage, FileUploadInterceptor), the OGNL/text-evaluation utilities (LocalizedTextUtil, TextParseUtil, OgnlValueStack, OgnlUtil, SecurityMemberAccess), the action-mapper/result paths (DefaultActionMapper, ServletActionRedirectResult), the REST plugin (ContentTypeInterceptor, DefaultContentTypeHandlerManager, XStreamHandler, struts-plugin.xml), struts-default.xml/struts-messages*.properties/default.properties, and the multipart/interceptor test suites. P1 index reports a partial index (163 of 1915 Java files parsed; syntax containment/call/inheritance candidates only; no data-flow, control-flow, semantic resolution, or runtime reachability; 50,906 unresolved calls), so index labels were treated only as navigation hints and every cited edge was re-checked in source text. Dependency jars referenced by the poms (notably commons-fileupload 1.3.2 and XStream 1.4.8) are binary artifacts outside the assigned tree and were not inspectable; the remaining ~2,600 files (view templates, CSS/JS, many plugins/apps) were only searched or spot-checked, not exhaustively read.
limitations: commons-fileupload 1.3.2 (the default 'jakarta' parser) is an external binary dependency; its exception messages could not be read here, so attacker control of the exception text for the default parser is inferred from the documented S2-045 defect rather than verified in this snapshot. The fully source-verified attacker-controlled variant uses the non-default jakarta-stream parser (struts.multipart.parser=jakarta-stream).
No code, tests, or exploit payloads were executed; the OGNL evaluation sink is established by source inspection of TextParseUtil.translateVariables/ValueStack, not runtime confirmation.

The P1 relation index is partial (163 parsed Java files of 1915; no data-flow/control-flow/reachability), and the review did not exhaustively read all 2666 files; view-layer templates, most plugin code, and application samples were only searched or spot-checked.

Repository metadata (git history, tags, issue references) is absent, so the exact fix commit/CVE identity for this snapshot could not be confirmed; the candidate is reported as a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Unrestricted XStream deserialization in REST plugin: plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/handler/XStreamHandler.java:43-50 calls new XStream().fromXML(in, target) on the raw request body, and ContentTypeInterceptor.java:52-65 feeds it the attacker-supplied body selected via the Content-Type header; the handler is registered by default in plugins/rest/src/main/resources/struts-plugin.xml:35 (S2-052 / CVE-2017-9805 style RCE).
rejected_leads.reason: Real and serious, but exploitability depends on the REST plugin being deployed and on a gadget chain being present in the application classpath (XStream 1.4.8, an external binary dependency that cannot be inspected here), so the attacker-control-to-impact evidence is weaker than the multipart/OGNL chain, which needs no external gadget. Left as an unconfirmed secondary lead.

rejected_leads.lead: OgnlUtil.getExcludedClasses()/getExcludedPackageNames() return live mutable collections (core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/ognl/OgnlUtil.java:116-126), which a sufficiently powerful OGNL expression can clear to bypass SecurityMemberAccess (the known S2-045 exploit primitive).
rejected_leads.reason: This is a hardening weakness that only matters after an OGNL injection already succeeded; it is not an independently reachable vulnerability and no injection into OgnlUtil was found.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultContentTypeHandlerManager.getHandlerForRequest can return null (plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/DefaultContentTypeHandlerManager.java:95-113) and ContentTypeInterceptor.java:64 dereferences it without a null check, giving a request-triggered NullPointerException.
rejected_leads.reason: Availability-only impact (at most a 500 response) and not competitive with the RCE-class candidate; not submitted as a second candidate per the one-candidate limit.

rejected_leads.lead: Index 'injection' hints in apps/showcase DAO classes (AbstractDao, EmployeeDao, TestDataProvider).
rejected_leads.reason: False positives: these lines are @Autowired field injections over an in-memory Storage implementation, not SQL/command construction from user input.

rejected_leads.lead: Potential OGNL evaluation in action/result parsing (DefaultActionMapper, ServletActionRedirectResult.conditionalParse, Freemarker/JSON plugins).
rejected_leads.reason: The snapshot already contains newer hardening here (allowedActionNames/allowedMethodNames with cleanupActionName/cleanupMethodName and tests asserting ${...}/%{...} payloads are replaced), so the pre-fix state for those fixes could not be established; left unconfirmed.

summary: Review of the Apache Struts snapshot (pom version 2.5.6-SNAPSHOT, commit dir 4759d2031d53f64726da) focused on the multipart/upload error path and other known Struts attack surfaces. I traced one candidate in depth: multipart parser error text that contains attacker-controlled data (exception messages carrying Content-Type / file name) is stored as a LocalizedMessage default message and later evaluated as an OGNL/variable expression by LocalizedTextUtil, yielding a remote code execution class of bug (the CVE-2017-5638 / S2-045–S2-046 defect family). All stages except the internal behavior of the commons-fileupload 1.3.2 dependency are verifiable in the assigned source. I also reviewed and rejected/left unconfirmed several other leads (unrestricted XStream XML handler in the REST plugin, mutable OGNL exclusion sets, a possible NPE DoS in the REST content-type selector).
